QUOTE: By default, a struct member written as `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(state)` is declared and named `private_state`. Code that reaches into `ssl->state` directly stops compiling, so the field is effectively private.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says that renaming the member to `private_state` enforces privacy at compile time. That is the member-name-breaking mechanism, though it never says the layout stays visible.
